items.headline: South Korea moves to approve abortion pills for the first time
items.summary: South Korea's government announced a plan to allow medication abortion up to nine weeks of pregnancy, with doctors able to prescribe the pills starting as early as next year. The move follows a 2019 constitutional court ruling that struck down the country's abortion ban, a ruling parliament had never followed up with new legislation.
items.why_it_matters: It ends a seven year legislative gap and gives South Korean women a safe, government sanctioned option to end a pregnancy for the first time.
